newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch TV producer Endemol's IPO to close earlier.
newsitem.headline: Dutch TV producer Endemol's IPO to close earlier.

text.p: The initial public offering of up to a third of the shares in Dutch television production firm Endemol Entertainment Holding NV is to be closed much earlier than initially expected, ABN AMRO Bank said on Monday.

ABN AMRO said subscriptions for retail and institutional investors in the Netherlands would now close on October 29 at 1400 GMT. Subscriptions for institutional investors outside the Netherlands were now expected to close on October 31 at 1400 GMT, it added.
ABN AMRO had said last Thursday that subscriptions were expected to close on November 6.
An ABN AMRO spokesman said the decision to close subscriptions earlier reflected strong demand for the shares.
ABN AMRO said last week that up to 9.69 million ordinary Endemol shares would be sold to investors in a combined primary and secondary offering at 44 to 48 guilders per share.
A book-building system is being used, with investors indicating the number of shares they want and the price they are willing to pay.
The price of the offering is now expected to be announced on Friday, November 1 with allocation of the shares and the first day of trading on the Amsterdam bourse slated for the same date.
Endemol was formed in 1994 by a merger of the production companies of co-chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol.
Endemol is one of Europe's biggest television production companies.
Its net profit rose 38 percent to 60.5 million guilders in the financial year to July 31, 1996 on a turnover of 642.4 million guilders.
The company expects net profit to rise by 15 to 20 percent in the current financial year to July 31, 1997, and predicts that both sales and profits will double within five years.
Endemol already generates some 40 percent of its turnover outside the Netherlands and plans further expansion abroad.
